subject: Isolation QA playbook and evidence checklist for private deployment
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Aline Dupont <aline.dupont@medforward.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jun 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Discovery — private deployment isolation items (follow-up)

Hi Aline — thanks again for the call earlier. I wanted to summarize the action items we discussed and make it concrete so your security and procurement teams have what they need. Short version: next steps below + ask for the SOC 2 evidence, a network diagram, and the partially completed vendor questionnaire.

Key takeaways from today's discovery:
- MedForward requires private-hosted inference (VPC) with network isolation and optional air-gapped/hardened mode for the QA environment.
- Regulatory concerns: HIPAA for PHI in production, GDPR for EU-sourced data; SOC 2 Type II is a gating control for the procurement checklist.
- Primary constraints: customer-managed KMS preferred, no public egress from model hosts, and audit logs retained for 12 months.

Immediate asks (can you confirm by EOD Friday?):
1) Current SOC 2 status & latest summary (attestations or in-progress timeline).
2) A network/topology sketch showing where you want Redwood components (private control plane? VPC peering? on-prem connector?).
3) The vendor security questionnaire we sent — we noted several fields missing; if you can return the file with the shaded answers we can pre-populate technical responses.

Technical notes for your security folk (Ben will join next call):
- We support private endpoints (no public IP), customer KMS, and private S3 access via VPC endpoints.
- For an air-gapped QA environment we typically deliver an appliance bundle + validated image and a documented evidence checklist.
- Network isolation options we propose: isolated VPC with NAT for only egress via approved proxy OR fully air-gapped with periodic sync via physical media.

Resources attached: SOC2_summary_2027.pdf (summary of Redwood controls), network_isolation_sketch.png (example topologies), vendor_questionnaire_responses.xlsx (blank copy).

Proposed next step: 30-minute technical follow-up on Tuesday (Solutions Architect + Sec Eng) to walk topology and finalize evidence list. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Kimberly
Kimberly Park

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Aline Dupont <aline.dupont@medforward.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — private deployment isolation items (follow-up)

Aline / team — thanks for the partial questionnaire and the constraints doc. A few clarifications from engineering so we all align before the Tuesday call: 

1) Public egress: yes, Redwood can be configured so that inference hosts have zero public IPs. All outbound traffic can be routed through a customer-controlled proxy or NAT gateway. We will not require public egress for model inference.

2) Air-gap delivery: we provide an image bundle + SHA256 checksums and a signing key (customer verifies signatures). For high-assurance builds we can also support a deterministic build record and SBOM export.

3) KMS: we support customer-managed KMS across AWS KMS and on-prem HSM integrations — key usage is limited to ciphertext operations (no plaintext key export).

4) Topology options (high level):
   - Option A (VPC-isolated hosted): Redwood model hosts in a private subnet, VPC endpoint to S3, customer-controlled KMS, control plane access via private peering.
   - Option B (Dedicated on-customer VPC): fully in your VPC, Redwood runtime runs on dedicated instances we provision into a customer subnet (preferred for strict isolation).
   - Option C (Air-gapped on-prem): appliance + validated images; periodic sync via signed payloads over physical media or controlled transfer node.

Can you confirm which option aligns with your procurement constraints? If you’d like, I’ll draft a minimal topology template (one-page) for you to drop into your architecture review.

On the BA: our legal team is ready to review once procurement shares the initial draft.

On Tue we should include our Sec Eng (I’ll invite Priya Natarajan from infra security) and Solutions Architect (Mateo Alvarez) — recommended 45 min so we can walk the topology and the vendor questionnaire line-by-line.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
